title: Programming & Flowcharts
description: Types of programming languages for programmable systems — text-based, block-based, and flowchart — and how.
content_html:
Programming a Programmable System

A programmable component such as a microcontroller does nothing useful until it is given a program — a precise sequence of instructions that tells it how to respond to inputs and control outputs. The specification identifies three types of programming language and system used to write or represent those instructions: text-based languages, block-based editors, and flowchart systems. Each has different characteristics, and the right choice depends on the complexity of the task and the experience of the programmer.

Text-Based Programming Languages

A text-based language requires the programmer to type instructions using the exact keywords and syntax of the chosen language — for example, C, MicroPython, or the Arduino language. Text-based code gives the greatest flexibility and control: any logic, however complex, can be expressed, and the resulting programs run efficiently on a microcontroller's processor. The disadvantage is the learning curve — syntax errors cause the program to fail, and beginners may find it hard to understand code written by others. Text-based code is the standard approach in professional and industrial engineering.

Key Fact

The three programming types are: text-based (written code, most powerful, steepest learning curve), block-based (drag-and-drop visual blocks, easier for beginners, limited for complex programs) and flowchart systems (visual symbols representing the flow of control, easy to plan and communicate, but can become complex to follow on large programs).

Block-Based Editors

Block-based editors such as Scratch or Microsoft MakeCode represent program instructions as graphical blocks that are dragged and snapped together on screen. Each block has a fixed shape that only allows valid connections, so syntax errors are almost impossible. This makes block-based editors highly accessible for beginners and for quickly prototyping simple control logic. The limitation is that complex logic quickly becomes cluttered and hard to follow, and not all programming concepts — particularly low-level hardware control — can be represented easily with pre-defined blocks. Block-based editors are widely used in schools and for rapid concept testing.

Text-based code transfers directly to professional and industrial settings — skills learned in Arduino C or Python are used in real engineering roles. Block-based editors, by contrast, are primarily educational tools. Some platforms such as MakeCode for the micro:bit allow the programmer to switch between block view and the equivalent text-based (Python or JavaScript) view of the same program, which helps learners make the transition. For the OCR exam, you need to understand the relative merits of each type and be able to argue which is more suitable for a given scenario — you are not expected to write actual code.

Flowchart Systems

A flowchart uses standardised shapes connected by arrows to represent the flow of control through a program. The key symbols are: an oval for start/end (terminal), a rectangle for a process step (such as 'turn LED on'), a diamond for a decision (a yes/no question), and a parallelogram for input or output. Flowchart software such as Flowol or PicLogicator can directly interpret a drawn flowchart as a program and run it on a connected programmable system. The advantage of flowcharts is that they make the logic of a program immediately visible, making them easy to plan, communicate, and debug. The disadvantage is that large, complex programs produce sprawling flowcharts that become difficult to read and maintain.

Key Fact

The four standard flowchart symbols are: oval — terminal (start/stop); rectangle — process (an action or calculation); diamond — decision (a yes/no question that creates a branch); parallelogram — input or output (e.g. reading a sensor or switching an output device). Arrows show the direction of flow between each step.

Using a Flowchart to Control a Programmable System

A flowchart directly models how a microcontroller or PLC executes a program. Consider a simple temperature alarm: the flowchart starts (oval), reads the temperature sensor (parallelogram — input), then reaches a decision diamond: 'Is temperature above 30°C?' If yes, an arrow leads to a process rectangle 'Turn on buzzer' and an output parallelogram; if no, an arrow loops back to read the sensor again. This loop continues indefinitely. The flowchart both communicates the design to other engineers and, in systems like Flowol, can be executed directly as the program itself. Identifying where decision diamonds create loops or branches is key to both drawing and interpreting flowcharts in the exam.

The choice of programming method depends on the experience of the programmer and the complexity of the task. For a beginner or for planning and communicating a simple control algorithm, flowcharts and block-based editors are the most accessible. For a complex, high-performance system that needs precise hardware control or efficient code, a text-based language is most appropriate. In an exam scenario question, always link your choice to the programmer's skill level, the complexity of the program required, and whether the code needs to be maintainable by others in a team.
exam_tip_html: Flowchart questions may ask you to complete, correct, or draw part of a flowchart. Always use the correct symbol shapes — drawing a process step as a diamond will lose marks. For 'compare' or 'discuss' questions about programming types, structure your answer around named advantages and disadvantages of each type, linked to the specific scenario in the question. A common mistake is describing what a flowchart looks like without explaining why the visual structure makes it easier to plan or debug a program compared with written code.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • The three programming types are text-based (powerful but demanding), block-based (accessible but limited), and flowchart systems (visual, easy to plan and communicate, but unwieldy for large programs).
  • The four standard flowchart symbols are oval (terminal), rectangle (process), diamond (decision), and parallelogram (input/output); arrows show the direction of program flow.
  • A flowchart can directly represent the control logic of a programmable system such as a microcontroller — decisions create branches and loops that mirror how the hardware responds to inputs.

glossary_terms.definition: A component such as a microcontroller or PLC that can be programmed to control a system's behaviour by executing a sequence of instructions.
A programming language where instructions are written as lines of typed code using a specific syntax, such as C, Python or Arduino's language.
A diagram that uses standard symbols — ovals, rectangles, diamonds, and parallelograms — to represent the sequence of steps and decisions in a program or process.
A visual programming environment where instructions are represented as graphical blocks that snap together, making syntax errors almost impossible.

practice_questions.text:
Which flowchart symbol is used to represent a decision — a point where the program branches based on a yes/no question?
A) Rectangle
B) Parallelogram
C) Oval
D) Diamond
State two advantages of using a block-based editor over a text-based programming language for a beginner programmer.
practice_questions.marks: One mark each for any two from: syntax errors are almost impossible because blocks only connect in valid ways / no need to remember exact keyword spelling or syntax / visual structure makes the program logic easier to follow / faster to produce a simple working program / less prior knowledge of programming required. [2 marks]

practice_questions.text: Explain one reason why a flowchart system is useful for designing the control program for a simple alarm circuit before the program is written.
practice_questions.marks: A simple point scores 1 mark (e.g. 'flowcharts show the order of steps visually'). Development scores 2 marks (e.g. 'a flowchart maps out all the decisions and loops in the program using standard symbols before any code is written, making the logic clear to both the designer and others'). A further developed point scores 3 marks (e.g. adding 'this means errors in the logic — such as a loop that never exits — can be spotted and corrected at the planning stage rather than after the program has been uploaded to the microcontroller, saving time and effort'). [3 marks]

practice_questions.text: Describe what a text-based programming language is and give one example of when it would be more suitable than a flowchart system.
practice_questions.marks: Description (up to 2 marks): a text-based language requires instructions to be typed using the exact syntax of the chosen language, such as C, Python or Arduino code — the programmer must know the correct keywords and structure (2 marks for a clear, complete description; 1 mark for a basic statement). Example (up to 2 marks): a text-based language would be more suitable when writing a complex, high-performance industrial control program where precise hardware control is needed and efficiency matters — for example, a PLC program managing a production line that must execute hundreds of steps per second (2 marks for a specific, applied example; 1 mark for a vague example). [4 marks total]

practice_questions.text:
A student is designing a control program for a greenhouse temperature monitoring system. The system must read a temperature sensor every five seconds and turn a fan motor on if the temperature exceeds 25°C, or off if it drops below 20°C.

Discuss which programming method — text-based, block-based, or flowchart — would be most suitable for this student to use.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (5-6 marks): A balanced discussion that recommends a specific method (most likely flowchart or block-based for this complexity level) with clear justification (e.g. the looping and two-decision logic maps well to a flowchart; a block-based editor prevents syntax errors for a less experienced programmer), and then considers why the other methods are less suitable (text-based requires syntax knowledge the student may lack; a pure flowchart cannot be executed without flowchart software). Both perspectives are developed with reasoning linked to the scenario.
Secure (3-4 marks): At least two relevant points with some justification linked to the scenario.
Developing (2 marks): One method identified with a basic reason.
Emerging (1 mark): A method named with no justification. [6 marks]

practice_questions.text: Evaluate the extent to which flowchart systems are the most effective method for programming a complex industrial programmable logic controller (PLC).
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (7-8 marks): A balanced evaluation that identifies clear strengths of flowcharts (visual logic, easy to plan and communicate, accessible for beginners, good for simple sequential programs) and then challenges these with well-developed limitations (large industrial programs produce sprawling, unmanageable flowcharts; text-based languages offer far greater control, efficiency, and scalability for complex tasks; professional engineers use text-based or ladder logic rather than flowcharts for PLCs). Considers specific scenarios where flowcharts are and are not appropriate. Reaches a substantiated conclusion that flowcharts are effective for design planning and simple programs but are not the most effective method for a complex industrial PLC.
Secure (5-6 marks): Strengths and limitations identified with some comparison and an attempt at a judgement.
Developing (3-4 marks): Points about flowcharts listed but limited comparison or no clear judgement.
Emerging (1-2 marks): Basic description with little evaluation. [8 marks]

knowledge_checks.q: Which flowchart symbol represents an input or output operation, such as reading a sensor value?
Which statement best describes a disadvantage of block-based editors compared with text-based languages?
options: Block-based editors always produce syntax errors
Block-based editors are limited in expressing complex logic and low-level hardware control
Block-based editors cannot be used with microcontrollers
Block-based editors require more programming knowledge than text-based languages

knowledge_checks.q: In a flowchart, a _____ shape (diamond) is used to represent a decision point where the program branches along a yes or no path.
Text-based programming languages give the greatest _____ and control but have the steepest learning curve of the three programming types.
Match each programming type to its most accurate description.
right: Drag-and-drop graphical blocks that snap together; syntax errors are almost impossible
Standard symbols connected by arrows represent the flow of control through a program
Instructions typed using exact syntax; most flexible but highest learning curve

flashcard_questions.q: Name the three types of programming language or system identified in the OCR specification.
flashcard_questions.a: The three types are text-based languages, block-based editors, and flowchart systems.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the main advantage of a text-based programming language over the other two types?
flashcard_questions.a: Text-based languages offer the greatest flexibility and control, allowing any level of complexity to be expressed and run efficiently on hardware.

flashcard_questions.q: Why are syntax errors almost impossible in a block-based editor?
flashcard_questions.a: Blocks are shaped so they only connect in valid ways, preventing a programmer from accidentally creating an illegal instruction combination.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the diamond symbol represent in a flowchart?
flashcard_questions.a: The diamond symbol represents a decision point — a yes/no question that causes the program to branch along two different paths.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the oval symbol represent in a flowchart?
flashcard_questions.a: The oval symbol represents a terminal — it marks the start or end point of the flowchart program.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the parallelogram symbol represent in a flowchart?
flashcard_questions.a: The parallelogram represents an input or output operation, such as reading a sensor value or turning on an output device.

flashcard_questions.q: Give one disadvantage of using a flowchart system for a large, complex program.
flashcard_questions.a: A large flowchart becomes sprawling and difficult to read or maintain, as the many arrows and symbols clutter the diagram significantly.

flashcard_questions.q: Give one example of a block-based editor used with microcontrollers.
flashcard_questions.a: Microsoft MakeCode is a block-based editor used to program the BBC micro:bit microcontroller in schools and for prototyping.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a flowchart system such as Flowol control a physical programmable system?
flashcard_questions.a: Flowol interprets the drawn flowchart directly as executable instructions and runs them on a connected programmable system automatically.

flashcard_questions.q: Which programming type is most commonly used in professional and industrial engineering?
flashcard_questions.a: Text-based programming languages are the standard in professional and industrial engineering because of their flexibility and efficiency.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is a flowchart useful for planning a control program before writing any code?
flashcard_questions.a: A flowchart makes the program logic visible using standard symbols, so errors in the logic can be identified and corrected before coding begins.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the rectangle symbol represent in a flowchart?
flashcard_questions.a: The rectangle represents a process step — an action or calculation the program performs, such as turning an LED on or adding two values.
